sanskrit: yasyoddhṛteṣv agniṣv ahute agnihotra evaṃ vidvān vrātyo 'tithiḥ | svayam enam abhyudetya brūyād vrātya kvāvātsīr iti vrātyo dakam iti vrātya tarpayantv iti ||
english: When the fires have been drawn out and the Agnihotra has not yet been offered, should a vrātya who knows thus arrive as a guest — one should go to meet him oneself and say: 'Vrātya, where have you dwelt?' 'Vrātya, let water be given,' 'Vrātya, let them refresh you.'

sanskrit: yad āha vrātya kvāvātsīr iti patha eva tena devayānān ava rundhe | (yad āha) vrātyodakam ity apa eva tenāva rundhe | yad āha vrātya tarpayantv iti prāṇam eva tena varṣāyāṃ saṃ kṛṇute ||
english: When he says 'Vrātya, where have you dwelt?' — by that he wins for him the paths that lead to the gods. When he says 'Vrātya, water!' — by that he wins water for him. When he says 'Vrātya, let them refresh you!' — by that he accumulates breath for him in the rainy season.

sanskrit: purāgnihotrasya havanād upāṃśu kṛṇvīta | vrātya yathā te priyaṃ tathāstv iti vrātya yathā te nikāmas tathāstv iti vrātya yathā te vaśastathāstv iti ||
english: Before the offering of the Agnihotra, one should perform it in a low murmur: 'Vrātya, may it be as is pleasing to you; Vrātya, may it be as is your desire; Vrātya, may it be as is your will.'

sanskrit: yad āha vrātya yathā te priyaṃ tathāstv iti priyam eva tenāva rundhe priye priyasya bhavaty ainaṃ priyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: When he says 'Vrātya, may it be as is pleasing to you' — by that he wins what is pleasing for him; he becomes the beloved of the beloved, and the pleasing goes to him — he who knows thus.

sanskrit: (yadāha vrātya yathā) te nikāmas tathāstv iti nikāmam eva tenāva rundhe nikāme nikāmam asya bhavaty ainaṃ nikāmo gacchati (ya evaṃ veda) | yad āha vrātya yathā te vaśas tathāstv iti vaśam eva tenāva rundhe vaśī vaśasya bhavaty ainaṃ vaśo gacchati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: When he says 'Vrātya, may it be as is your desire' — by that he wins desire for him; his desire is fulfilled in desire, and desire comes to him — he who knows thus. When he says 'Vrātya, may it be as is your will' — by that he wins will for him; he becomes master of what is his will, and will comes to him — he who knows thus.

sanskrit: yasyādhiśrite agnihotra evaṃ vidvān vrātyo 'tithir gṛham āgacchet | svayam enam abhyudetya brūyād vrātyāti sṛja hoṣyāmīti | ati ca sṛjej juhūyān na cātisṛjen na juhūyāt | yo vā evaṃ viduṣā vrātyenānatisṛṣṭo juhoti | na devayānaṃ panthāṃ pra jānāti na pitṛyāṇam ā deveṣu vṛścate 'hutam asya bhavati | yo vā evaṃ viduṣā vrātyenānatisṛṣṭo juhoti | pra devayānaṃ panthāṃ jānāti pra pitṛyānaṃ pary asyāsmim̐l loka āyatanaṃ śiṣyate hutam asya bhavati ||
english: When the Agnihotra fire is kindled and a vrātya who knows thus comes to someone's house as a guest — one should go to meet him oneself and say: 'Vrātya, grant leave; I shall offer.' And if he grants leave, one should offer; if he does not grant leave, one should not offer. Whoever offers without being granted leave by a vrātya who knows thus — he does not know the path to the gods nor the path to the fathers; he is cut off among the gods; his offering is as if not offered. But whoever, having been granted leave by a vrātya who knows thus, then offers — he knows the path to the gods and the path to the fathers; a resting place remains for him in this world; his offering is truly offered.

sanskrit: yasyaivaṃ vidvān vrātya ekāṃ rātrim atithir gṛhe vasati | ye pṛthivyāṃ puṇyā lokās tān evainenāva rundhe ||
english: In whose house a vrātya who knows thus stays as a guest for one night — he thereby wins for him all the meritorious worlds that are in the earth.

sanskrit: (yasyaivaṃ vidvān) vrātyo dvitīyāṃ rātriṃ (atithir gṛhe vasati) | ye antarikṣe puṇyā lokās (tān evainenāva rundhe) ||
english: In whose house a vrātya who knows thus stays as a guest for a second night — he thereby wins for him all the meritorious worlds that are in the atmosphere.

sanskrit: (yasyaivaṃ vidvān) vrātyas tṛtīyāṃ rātriṃ (atithir gṛhe vasati) | ye divi puṇyā lokās (tān evainenāva rundhe) ||
english: In whose house a vrātya who knows thus stays as a guest for a third night — he thereby wins for him all the meritorious worlds that are in the sky.

sanskrit: (yasyaivaṃ vidvān) vrātyaś catūrthīṃ rātrim ātithiḥ (gṛhe vasati) | sarvān evainena puṇyām̐l lokān ava rundhe ||
english: In whose house a vrātya who knows thus stays as a guest for a fourth night — he thereby wins for him all meritorious worlds entirely.

sanskrit: (yasyaiva vidvān) vrātyaḥ pañcamīṃ rātrim atithiḥ (gṛhe vasati) | parāvata evainena lokān ava (rundhe) ||
english: In whose house a vrātya who knows thus stays as a guest for a fifth night — he thereby wins worlds at the farthest distance.

sanskrit: yasyaivaṃ vidvān vrātyo 'parimitā rātrīr atithir gṛhe vasati | aparimitān evainena lokān ava rundhe ||
english: In whose house a vrātya who knows thus stays as a guest for an unlimited number of nights — he thereby wins unlimited worlds.
